bounded_question: What does the full record-write entry 0x5f0f930 do end to end on node #115: how is the internal key built, how are the two product lookups resolved, what does the virtual dispatch at owner slot 0x40 do with its three once-helper sites, when does the grow path run, when does ProtectionInfo validation run and fail, and how does the arm-2 path reach the 0x5f0e890 insert from #3330?

key_build_0x5eab0c0.inline: inline buffer iff len(key)+len(second)+13 <= 0xc8 (200), else operator new
key_build_0x5eab0c0.layout: varint(len(key)+8) + key + [second slice] + trailer ((tag<<8)|0x16, 8 LE bytes)
key_build_0x5eab0c0.minus_0x150_slice: the -0x150 record is {data, total-8}: the built key minus its 8-byte trailer (varint prefix + user key). It is the slice the bucket projection, the product-2 check, the arm-1 fold's fourth hash and the resolve's second slice all read. It is an out-parameter of the product-1 slot-0x30 call, overwritten with {data, total-8} before any read.

key_len_0x5f06f40.behavior: parses the varint after the trailer and returns (value length, value ptr)

main_0x5f0f930.args: rdi = out Status* (16 bytes), rsi = owner, rdx = tag qword, rcx = pointer to the key slice record {ptr, len}, r8 = pointer to the options slice record {ptr, len}, r9 = direct pointer or null

dispatch_arms.1: once helper at 0x5f0fce4. If reported_len < vlen, grow: re-encode varint(reported_len) at the value-varint position; when varint_len(vlen) > varint_len(reported_len) the value bytes shift with memcpy. Stats slot 0xb0 code 0x27 on owner+0x50 if non-null. If r9 non-null: fold = *(r9) ^ H(tag, 0x77a00858ddd37f21) ^ H(trailer>>8, 0x77a00858ddd37f21) ^ H(options, 0xd28aad72f49bd50b) ^ H(-0x150 slice, 0xd28aad72f49bd50b); resolve 0x5f09e90 with value_ptr=&fold (direct path), first_slice=orig-rcx, second_slice=-0x150, byte_in=1, qword_in=trailer>>8, out_slot=value_ptr+reported_len, stored truncated to owner+0x6c width; then validate 0x5f09b10 with buffer = the found record [0, value_end), capacity = *(*(owner+0x10)+0x28), protection=fold; out = validate status (Corruption code 2 + one of 7 messages on failure). If r9 null: resolve runs its own four-way fold and out={0} with no validate.
dispatch_arms.2: once helper at 0x5f0ff5e. fold2 = *(r9) ^ H(options, 0xd28aad72f49bd50b) ^ H(dispatch out-string, 0xd28aad72f49bd50b); insert 0x5f0e890 (#3330) at 0x5f0ff12 with out=&-0x150 (reused slot), owner, keypart=tag, type=1, part1=orig-rcx slice, part2=dispatch out-string slice, arg7=&fold2 (or NULL when r9 null, in which case insert runs its own hash path and validate is skipped), flag=0, context=NULL, counters=NULL. Insert status move-assigned -0x150 -> temp -0x170 -> out via 0x5f05310 twice; the two delete[] checks after each move find null (the move already zeroed the source) and are no-ops. Stats slot 0xb0 code 0x25; once; out = insert status (OK, TryAgain 13 'key+seq exists', or Corruption).
dispatch_arms.other: any other dispatch code returns NotFound (code 1).

phases: 1. Key build 0x5eab0c0: internal key = varint(len+8) + key + trailer ((tag<<8)|0x16).

2. Product-1 lookup on owner+0xa50: slot 0x98 vs GOT 0x64ed778 (0x5f04d80, #3286's forwarder); canonical calls slot 0x90 instead. Then slot 0x30, slot 0x10 (must be true, else NotFound), slot 0x18 returns the found key bytes.
3. Found-key parse: first byte < 0x80 or varint32 0x61bd4f0; trailer = qword at payload + klen - 8; low byte must be 1 (kTypeValue), else NotFound.

4. Product-2 lookup on owner+0x10: slot 0x98 vs GOT 0x64ed010 (0x5d2ca80); canonical calls slot 0x10 on the product+0x20 subobject. Opposite return senses: the canonical slot 0x10 proceeds on return 0, the non-canonical slot 0x98 proceeds on nonzero return.
5. Value length 0x5f06f40 at trailer + 8, bucket projection 0x5f099b0 on the -0x150 slice, bucket write-lock 0x60d5ab0.
6. Dispatch call *0x40(%r12) with (value ptr, &-0x17c reported-length inout, options record by value, &-0x140 out string, orig r9); returns 0, 1 or 2.

7. Epilogue (dispatch arms only): bucket unlock 0x60d5c30, out-string _M_dispose, product-1 release (slot 0x8 on rbx), key-buffer delete[] iff heap-allocated. Early-NotFound paths skip the lock/unlock and the dispose (the string is empty SSO there).

resolve_0x5f09e90.behavior: direct path (value_ptr non-null): the resolved value is the qword at value_ptr, no hash call. Fold path (null): value = H(first, 0) ^ H(second, 0xd28aad72f49bd50b) ^ H(byte, 0xa5155ae5e937aa16) ^ H(qword, 0x77a00858ddd37f21). The value is stored truncated to the host+0x6c width (1/2/4/8 bytes); width 0 or outside {1,2,4,8} stores nothing.

rwlock.rc_rule: rc in {0, 0x10, 0x6e} accepted, else fprintf(stderr, "pthread %s: %s\n", "write lock" / "write unlock", strerror) then _M_dispose + abort

unknowns: The concrete callee of the owner's virtual slot 0x40 and the exact C++ meaning of dispatch codes 0/1/2 are inferred from the arms, not proven from this window alone.

The -0x17c inference: the dispatch receives &-0x17c; arm 1 compares post-call -0x17c against -0x1f0 (vlen). The grow path is reachable exactly when the dispatch writes a smaller length there; whether it writes is inferred from the comparison, not proven from this window alone.
A found-key varint failure returns 0 in the binary (the window would then read at payload+len-8 with a null pointer); the model raises ValueError instead.
The single caller 0x5fc6433 (FDE 0x5fc6070..0x5fc6e8b) is not pinned here: what it is, and what it passes as the key/tag/options/direct arguments, is the next open question.
